claims.text: Other recommended IV regimens: cefotetan 2 g IV q12h or cefoxitin 2 g IV q6h, each + doxycycline 100 mg PO/IV q12h;
claims.quote: Cefotetan 2 g IV every 12 hours plus Doxycycline 100 mg orally or IV every 12 hours or Cefoxitin 2 g IV every 6 hours plus Doxycycline 100 mg orally or IV every 12 hours

claims.text: give doxycycline orally when possible (IV infusion is painful)
claims.quote: Because of the pain associated with IV infusion, doxycycline should be administered orally when possible.

claims.text: Alternative IV regimens: ampicillin-sulbactam 3 g IV q6h + doxycycline; or clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h + gentamicin (2 mg/kg load, then 1.5 mg/kg q8h, or 3–5 mg/kg once daily)
claims.quote: Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 g IV every 6 hours plus Doxycycline 100 mg orally or IV every 12 hours or Clindamycin 900 mg IV every 8 hours plus Gentamicin loading dose IV or IM (2 mg/kg body weight), followed by a maintenance dose (1.5 mg/kg body weight) every 8 hours; single daily dosing (3–5 mg/kg body weight) can be substituted

claims.text: Other IM/oral regimens: cefoxitin 2 g IM + probenecid 1 g PO, or another parenteral third-generation cephalosporin, each + doxycycline + metronidazole x14 days
claims.quote: Cefoxitin 2 g IM in a single dose and probenecid 1 g orally administered concurrently in a single dose plus Doxycycline 100 mg orally 2 times/day for 14 days with metronidazole 500 mg orally 2 times/day for 14 days or Other parenteral third-generation cephalosporin (e.g., ceftizoxime or cefotaxime) plus Doxycycline 100 mg orally 2 times/day for 14 days with metronidazole 500 mg orally 2 times/day for 14 days

claims.text: Cephalosporin allergy with low gonorrhea risk: levofloxacin 500 mg or moxifloxacin 400 mg PO daily + metronidazole x14 days, or azithromycin + metronidazole;
claims.quote: However, if the patient has cephalosporin allergy, the community prevalence and individual risk for gonorrhea are low, and follow-up is likely, alternative therapy can be considered. Use of either levofloxacin 500 mg orally once daily or moxifloxacin 400 mg orally once daily with metronidazole 500 mg orally 2 times/day for 14 days (1179–1181) or azithromycin 500 mg IV daily for 1–2 doses, followed by 250 mg orally daily in combination with metronidazole 500 mg 2 times/day for 12–14 days (1178), can be considered.

claims.text: quinolone regimens otherwise aren't recommended (resistant N. gonorrhoeae)
claims.quote: As a result of the emergence of quinolone-resistant N. gonorrhoeae, regimens that include a quinolone agent are not recommended for PID treatment.

claims.text: Metronidazole adds anaerobic coverage and also treats BV, which often accompanies PID
claims.quote: The addition of metronidazole to these regimens provides extended coverage against anaerobic organisms and will also effectively treat BV, which is frequently associated with PID.
